rgb: The scene is viewed from a steeply downward-angled egocentric perspective on a narrow wooden boardwalk flanked by low vegetation on both the right and left. At the bottom of the frame, about 3 to 5 metres away and out of reach, the camera wearer's dark-gloved right hand and bare left hand hold a small wrapped bar above a blue plastic poncho or sheet. Standing on the right edge of the boardwalk about 3 to 5 metres in front of the camera wearer is a person in a blue jacket and yellow vest whose torso faces away from the camera wearer and whose bare left hand extends palm-up to about 3 to 5 metres—out of reach of both individuals—while all heads and faces are cropped out above the top of the frame, making eye gaze unobservable. Two other people are partially visible far away on the left side of the boardwalk: one in a dark poncho and black leggings who is about 3 to 5 metres in front in the first frame (about 3 to 5 metres to the left of the blue-jacketed person), and another in jeans and a translucent yellow poncho about 3 to 5 metres to the left in the second frame and at the bottom-left corner in the third through fifth frames. In the first two frames, the camera wearer's blue plastic sheet and the dark poncho occlude most of the boardwalk, but from the second to the fourth frame the dark-ponchoed person approaches along the boardwalk to within about 0.5 to 1.0 metres and mostly enters from the top edge while the blue plastic sheet drops to the bottom margin, exposing the wooden planks below. Across the five frames, the person in the blue jacket remains stationary with their left hand extended while the camera wearer's hands move away from 3 metres to 5 metres to bring the wrapped bar into contact with that outstretched palm in the third and fourth frames, before the camera wearer's right gloved hand moves forward slightly in the fifth frame.
depth: The depth map captures the downward-sloping outdoor scene on a wooden boardwalk (~3–5 m below eye level) flanked by recessed vegetation, with the camera wearer's hands and blue poncho in the brightest distant region (~3–5 m) at the bottom. A person in a blue jacket and yellow vest stands directly in front and slightly right (~3–5 m away, head cropped above the frame) facing away from the camera wearer, while a second person in a dark poncho approaches down the boardwalk from ~3–5 m in frame 1 to ~0.5–1.0 m in frame 2 (occluded behind the first person in frames 3–4) and a third person in a yellow poncho stands ~3–5 m to the left (~3–5 m from the first person, partially out of view at the left edge). Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's gloved right hand and bare left hand move away to meet the first person's outstretched left hand out of arm's reach (~3–5 m) to pass a small snack bar, before the camera wearer's right hand moves forward slightly in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradients clearly separate the overlapping hands and arms from the boardwalk and vegetation beneath them and show the relative elevation of the raised hands above the ground plane. However, the map is unreliable in scale consistency across frames—such as the first person's shoulder abruptly saturating to bright white in frame 2 while appearing mid-grey in frame 3 despite minimal distance change—and it merges the snack bar into the surrounding hand surfaces.
segmentation: The segmentation map labels portions of the people on the boardwalk against an unlabelled black background, showing the camera wearer's hands and poncho at the bottom (~3–5 m), the outward-facing person in the blue jacket in the upper-right/centre (~3–5 m), the approaching person's legs above them in frames 2 and 5 (~0.5–1.0 m), and the third person on the left edge (~3–5 m away and ~3–5 m from the central person). While the map outlines the spatial divergence of the camera wearer's hands and the first person's extended left arm out of reach (~3–5 m) in frames 3–5, all heads remain cropped above the top edge so gaze direction cannot be determined. It makes the nearby, dark legs of the approaching person at the top of frames 2 and 5 easier to isolate as distinct human instances than in the dark RGB shadows. However, the map is highly unreliable for instance separation and class accuracy: it omits the boardwalk, vegetation, and handheld snack bar entirely, misses the camera wearer's hands in frame 2, splits the blue-jacketed person into separate masks for their jacket and yellow vest in frame 2, and merges the camera wearer's right arm and the first person's body into a single cyan mask across an arbitrary horizontal seam in frames 3 and 4. Furthermore, in frame 5 it falsely classifies the camera wearer's dark-gloved right hand as a 'bird' while fragmenting the overlapping arms and left-side person into inconsistent mask pieces.
pose: The pose map renders only isolated 2D hand skeletons in magenta on a completely black background, omitting all yellow body skeletons, scene layout, background objects, and head/torso orientations across all 5 frames. In frames 1 to 3, it detects only the extended left hand of the blue-jacketed person located in front and to the right of the camera wearer (~3–5 m away, out of reach), showing the open palm facing upward and outward as it lowers slightly toward the bottom-centre while moving away from the camera wearer's hands. In frame 4, it detects both the first person's open left hand and the camera wearer's left hand (~3–5 m away, touching at the centre-left) as the snack bar is transferred, before failing to detect any hands at all in frame 5 even though both remain clearly visible in the RGB image. Compared to RGB alone, the magenta keypoints explicitly articulate the five finger joints and palm orientation of the extended hand in frames 1–2 and the opposing thumb-and-finger grasp of the camera wearer's left hand in frame 4. However, the map is severely incomplete because heavy top-down foreshortening, cropped heads and torsos, and mutual occlusion by the dark glove and snack bar cause it to miss all three surrounding bodies, the camera wearer's gloved right hand in every frame, and the camera wearer's left hand in frames 1–3 and 5.
